effect-glimpse-desc: See your own dice this turn.
effect-swap-desc: Trade your whole hand with a player.
effect-ward-desc: Nothing can make you draw until your next turn.

hand-hint: Tap a card to see what it does. A caught lie costs {{penalty}}.
hand-locked: Cards are played on your own turn, before you roll.
horn-sounded: The horn has sounded. Last turns.
house-rules-by-fallback: Balanced locally — the AI was unavailable.
house-rules-hint: Say what is wrong with the game and it will be balanced for you — “the horn is too risky”, “games drag on”, “drop Scry”.
house-rules-offline: Could not reach the server. Try again in a moment.
leaderboard-empty: Nobody has finished a game yet. Go first.
leaderboard-error: The record is unavailable right now.

log-end: {{actor}} sounded the horn. One turn each, then hands are counted.
log-glimpse: {{actor}} bought a look at the dice.
need-ready: Waiting on the table to be ready.
no-tables: Nobody is hosting right now. Host one and send the code around.
phase-action-you: Your turn. Play cards, then roll.
phase-claim-them: {{name}} cannot see the dice. Tell them a total.
pitch: Three dice, and you are the one person who cannot see them. Ask the table. Decide who is lying. Whoever ends holding the fewest cards wins.
play-cost: Costs you {{draw}} cards for the one you spend — net one worse.
player-range: {{min}}–{{max}} players. Bluffing works better with more of them.
results-backfired: {{name}} sounded the horn without being strictly lowest, so the call backfired and drops them to last.
rules-away-1: Losing signal does not lose you the game. Your seat, your cards and your place in the order are held for about {{seconds}} seconds, and coming back — reconnecting, or reloading the page — puts you straight back in them.
rules-away-2: The table does not wait, though. While you are away your turns are skipped and your answers default to the truth, so nobody is stuck watching a clock run down on somebody who is not there.
rules-cards-1: Everyone starts with {{start}}. Drawing is never one card: the card you drew brings two more, so being caught costs {{penalty}}.
rules-cards-2: Playing a card is a discard, and a discard draws {{draw}} — so every card you use leaves you one card worse off. Use one anyway when it costs somebody else three.
rules-cards-3: Your own cards are always yours to look at. Cards are played on your own turn, before you roll.
rules-clock-1: Every phase is timed, and every timeout has a defined outcome rather than a stall: {{action}}s to play cards and roll, {{claim}}s to say a number, {{call}}s to make the call.
rules-clock-2: Say nothing and you are recorded as having told the TRUTH — silence is never scored as a lie. Let the call run out and the roller draws, because they had the whole phase to make one.
rules-colors-intro: Rank means nothing. Colour means everything.
rules-end-1: On your turn, instead of rolling, you may call the End. Everyone else then takes one last turn — cards only, no dice — and hands are counted.
rules-end-2: Fewest cards wins. But whoever sounded the horn has to be strictly lowest: tie the field or lose to it and the call backfires, and they finish last however few cards they are holding.
rules-end-3: Which is why that last turn is dangerous. The player sitting on a seven can still take your three-card hand off you.
rules-seven-desc: the one rank that matters: trade your entire hand with anyone you like. It ignores the colour.
rules-table-1: {{min}} to {{max}} players. Everyone can see how many cards everyone else is holding — that is the score, and hiding it would hide the race. What is in those hands is private.
rules-table-3: Talk to each other. The numbers are the only structured part of a claim — the persuading, the pattern-spotting and the outright lying happen in the chat, and a bluffing game without it is a coin flip.
rules-table-4: One deck of {{deck}} — four colours, thirteen ranks. When it runs out the discards are shuffled back in, so it never actually runs dry.
rules-turn-1: Three dice are rolled and you are the only person at the table who cannot see them. Everyone else can.
rules-turn-2: Each of them tells you a total. They may tell the truth or they may not. You pick one of them and call it — truth, or lie.
rules-turn-3: Right, and they draw {{penalty}}. Wrong, and you draw {{penalty}}.
sign-in-required: Gabriel’s Horn is played against other people, so it needs an account.
sound-horn-hint: You must be strictly lowest when the counting stops.
title: Gabriel’s Horn
